svg.title: Figure 4-1 · Operating modes and actuation authority
svg.desc: State diagram of the WP-C-01 §4 operating modes: Off / offroad (actuation: none); Onroad, disengaged (actuation: none); Pre-enabled / enabled (actuation: lateral, longitudinal); Overriding (actuation: lateral, no longitudinal); Soft disabling (actuation: lateral, longitudinal (forced decel)); Immediate disable (actuation: none); Driver lockout (actuation: none). Transitions carry the record IDs H:D1, H:D2, H:D3, H:E1, H:E2, H:N1, H:O1, H:O2, H:SD1, H:SD2, H:X1, H:X2, P:M2, P:M4, P:M5, P:M7, P:T1, P:T10a, P:T10b, P:T10c, P:T11, P:T2, P:T3, P:T4, P:T5, P:T6, P:T7, P:T8. Engagement (D1/D3, T1) and driver disengagement (X2, T2/T3) and envelope faults are enforced by the panda envelope; override (E2/O2), immediate disable (X1) and the lockout are host only; soft disabling (E1, O1, SD2) is host only while the envelope keeps controls_allowed = 1 (GAP-16). Configuration: Chill, Experimental (upstream default, GAP-18), debug modes excluded (OI-5).
svg.text: Figure 4-1 · Operating modes and actuation authority
The §4 modes as one state diagram. Each arrow names the state-machine record transitions it stands for and is coloured by who enforces it.
after the PCM cruise rising edge, no NO_ENTRY
critical fault; control released at once
H: X2 · P: T2, T3 clear
P: T4 T5 T10a · ref.: T10b T10c T11
P: T2 after cancel, or T6
CONFIGURATION · selected before driving, not states (§4 rows)
upstream default (params_keys.h:43) · GAP-18 · in ODD? OI-8
enforced by the panda envelope (P); the host (H) also acts
host only while the envelope still allows actuation (GAP-16)
Record IDs: H = sm-selfdrived; P = sm-toy-auth (T), sm-safety-mode (M).
Envelope clears the record lists as not implemented, so not drawn as enforcement: T9 T10d T10e T12 T13 T14 T15.
Nothing here is verified; it is the design as WP-C-01 §4 and the records state it. The lockout and the 3 s timer exist only on the host; the envelope does not know them.
